sessions.prompt:
Add parse_line(line) to parse.py. A log line looks like 2026-06-01 12:00:05 INFO GET /home 200 35ms (date, time, level, method, path, status, duration). parse_line returns a dict with the keys date, time, hour, level, method, path, status (int) and ms (int). Add tests.

The plan for parse_line has one more step: the duration may also be in seconds ("1.2s" is 1200 ms). Do not do that step now; leave it for a later session.

Project rule (it applies to all later work too): parse_line raises ValueError for a malformed line, and any function that takes many lines skips the malformed ones.

Design decision for this project: a slow request is one that takes more than 500 ms.

given.handoff: Session 1 added parse_line(line) with tests. Its last step is left for later: durations in seconds.
decisions: parse_line raises ValueError for a malformed line; functions that take many lines skip malformed ones.
A slow request takes more than 500 ms.

sessions.prompt:
Add parse_lines(lines) to parse.py: the records of all lines. Add count_levels(records) to stats.py: a dict from level to number of records. Add tests.

Project rule (it applies to all later work too): methods ignore case and are stored in upper case ("get" becomes "GET").

Design decision for this project: an error is a request with status 500 or above.

Design decision for this project: each path line of a report has the form /home 12.

given.handoff: Session 2 added parse_lines and count_levels with tests.
decisions: Methods ignore case and are stored upper case.
An error is a request with status 500 or above.
A report path line has the form /home 12.

sessions.prompt:
Add error_rate(records) to stats.py: the percent of requests that are errors. Add tests.

Change to an earlier decision (it replaces the old one): an error is a request with status 400 or above, not 500.

Design decision for this project: requests to /health are ignored by every statistic and by the report.

Design decision for this project: error_rate is rounded to one decimal (1 error in 3 requests is 33.3).

decisions: Supersedes 500: an error is a request with status 400 or above.
Requests to /health are ignored by every statistic and by the report.
error_rate is rounded to one decimal.

sessions.prompt:
Add top_paths(records, n) to stats.py: the n most requested paths as (path, count) pairs, most first. Add tests.

The plan for top_paths has one more step: a query string is removed before counting ("/a?x=1" counts as "/a"). Do not do that step now; leave it for a later session.

Change to an earlier decision (it replaces the old one): a slow request is one that takes more than 300 ms, not 500.

given.handoff: Session 4 added top_paths(records, n) with tests. Its last step is left for later: strip query strings.
decisions: Supersedes 500 ms: a slow request takes more than 300 ms.

given.handoff: Session 5 added by_hour(records) with tests. Its last step is left for later: include empty hours between first and last with 0.
